mechanism.plausibility_rationale: Thiazide diuretics can cause acute kidney injury primarily through two mechanisms: pre-renal azotemia due to excessive volume depletion and, less commonly, acute interstitial nephritis as an idiosyncratic hypersensitivity reaction. While they are generally nephroprotective in the long term, the risk of acute functional decline is well-documented, particularly in patients with pre-existing renal impairment or those on concomitant RAAS inhibitors.
